title: Mirra Andreeva wins her first WTA Finals without dropping a set
subtitle: At 19, Andreeva is the youngest winner since Maria Sharapova in 2004. In the final, Elina Svitolina made her work for a first set that had seemed within reach.
author: ATHENA

paragraphs.text: Mirra Andreeva had the first set on her racket at 5–4 when she served two double faults and sent a backhand long. Elina Svitolina was level again. Two games later, the 19-year-old Russian had broken Svitolina’s serve and held her own to take the set 7–5. She won the second 6–3 on Sunday at Indian Wells to claim the WTA Finals title on her singles debut.

It was Andreeva’s fifth win in five matches at the season-ending championship, all in straight sets. No teenager had lifted the singles trophy since Maria Sharapova in 2004. The unbeaten run earned Andreeva the maximum prize of $3.37 million and took her to a career-high No. 2 in the world rankings.

The first time Andreeva beat Svitolina that week, 6–4, 6–0 in the group stage, she surprised her coach, Conchita Martínez, by asking to go back out and practise. She wanted to hit a few serves and loosen up her strokes, she told the WTA. The two had already worked through one major final together this year: in Paris, Andreeva beat Polish qualifier Maja Chwalińska for her first Grand Slam singles title.

By the time the finalists met again, Svitolina had beaten Karolína Muchová, Aryna Sabalenka and Wimbledon champion Linda Nosková. Andreeva and Martínez expected a different match. Andreeva later told reporters she had used her warm-up to practise what she would say to herself after a miss: she would make the next shot. She kept that routine when the match began.

Svitolina, 32, gave herself 12 chances to break serve in the final but converted only three. Andreeva broke her six times. Even late in the second set, Svitolina held serve through six deuces to bring the score to 4–3. Andreeva held in reply, then won the title when Svitolina put an overhead into the net.

For the Ukrainian, who won the event in 2018, this was a first appearance at the Finals since 2019 and a third trip to the title match. She had won in Auckland and Rome this season. After Sunday’s final, she said she hoped her return to this level after pregnancy would encourage other women in sport.

Andreeva finished the season with four titles and 55 match wins, more wins than any other player on the tour. A year earlier she had been a singles alternate at the Finals and never played a point. This time she left with the Billie Jean King Trophy, with King herself in the stands.
